Land Transport and Related Matters Bill, Second Reading debate

Second Reading3 February 2026 – 4 February 2026 bill-780, bill-781

A Second Reading debate on the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill, an omnibus Bill by the Ministry of Transport and Ministry of Home Affairs that amends road traffic, active mobility, ERP 2.0, speed limiter and related laws.

The Bill decriminalises missed ERP charges and makes the On-Board Unit mandatory for all Singapore-registered vehicles from 1 January 2027. It lowers the speed limit for mobility vehicles on public paths to six kilometres an hour from 1 June 2026, requires a Certificate of Medical Need for mobility scooter users on public paths, and introduces registration and penalties. It also raises penalties for illegal vehicle modifications and unregistered or deregistered vehicles, and updates speed limiter offences.

      Verbatim
      The Land Transport and Related Matters Bill is an omnibus Bill that regularises provisions across several existing Acts.

    • Clauses 59 to 64 simplify settlement processes and decriminalise missed ERP charges.

      Verbatim
      This is why we are introducing clauses 59 to 64 in this Bill to simplify settlement processes and to decriminalise missed ERP charges, which are currently an offence under the Road Traffic Act.

    • From 1 January 2027, the OBU will be mandatory for all Singapore-registered vehicles when ERP 2.0 is fully rolled out and ERP 1.0 is decommissioned.

      Verbatim
      On 1 January 2027, when the ERP 2.0 is completely rolled out and ERP 1.0 is decommissioned, the OBU will be mandatory for all Singapore-registered vehicles.

    • Remaining vehicle owners get another three months to install OBUs at no cost.

      Verbatim

    • Distance-based charging will not be introduced in the immediate term.

      Verbatim
      This means that we will not be introducing distance-based charging in the immediate term.

    • Serious cases of deliberate non-compliance or misuse of OBUs carry penalties of up to $20,000 and/or imprisonment up to two years.

      Verbatim

    • Clause 52 raises maximum penalties for illegal vehicle alterations.

      Verbatim

    • Individuals can face fines up to $20,000 and/or imprisonment up to two years for illegal alterations, doubled for repeat offenders.

      Verbatim

    • Clause 57 increases penalties for keeping or using unregistered or deregistered vehicles.

      Verbatim

Motion to lift speaking limits for the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill

Second Reading3 February 2026 motion-2799

A procedural motion moved by the Leader of the House, and assented to by the Speaker and Members present, exempting two office-holders from the Standing Orders so they may speak more than once and without time limits during the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill.

The record does not set out the practical impact.

  • The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)

    • The Leader of the House asked for consent and general assent to exempt the proceedings from Standing Order No 48(3), so that Senior Minister of State Ms Sim Ann and Minister of State Mr Baey Yam Keng may speak more than once in the Second Reading debate.

      Verbatim

    • She also asked to be exempted from Standing Order No 48(8) to remove the time limits on those two speeches, saying their speeches may not finish within the time limit.

      Verbatim
      I am asking to lift the time limit in respect of their speeches.

    • Acting Minister Jeffrey Siow will move the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill and will speak on the amendments on the Electronic Road Pricing 2.0 system and serious vehicular offences.

      Verbatim
      Acting Minister Jeffrey Siow will be moving the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill and will speak on the amendments pertaining to the Electronic Road Pricing 2.0 system and serious vehicular offences.

    • Minister of State Mr Baey Yam Keng will speak on the active mobility related amendments.

      Verbatim
      Minister of State Mr Baey Yam Keng will speak on the active mobility related amendments

    • Senior Minister of State Ms Sim Ann, on behalf of the Minister for Home Affairs, will speak on the new offences and increased penalties relating to speed limiters and other miscellaneous amendments.

      Verbatim
      Senior Minister of State Ms Sim Ann, on behalf of the Minister for Home Affairs, will speak on the new offences and increase in penalties relating to the speed limiters and other miscellaneous amendments.

  • Mr Speaker

    • The Speaker gave his consent to the motion.

      Verbatim
      I give my consent.

    • The exemption was resolved: the proceedings are exempted from Standing Order No 48(3) so the two office-holders may speak more than once, and from Standing Order 48(8) to remove the time limits on their speeches for the Second Reading of the Bill.

      Verbatim
      That the proceedings under discussion be exempted from the provisions of Standing Order No 48(3) to enable Senior Minister of State Ms Sim Ann and Minister of State Mr Baey Yam Keng to speak more than once for the Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill

What happens next The Second Reading of the Land Transport and Related Matters Bill proceeds, with Acting Minister Jeffrey Siow moving it, and with Senior Minister of State Ms Sim Ann and Minister of State Mr Baey Yam Keng able to speak more than once and without time limits.

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • What the new offences and increased penalties relating to speed limiters will be, and when they take effect.

  • When the Bill, if passed, is intended to come into force.

Adjournment Motion on strengthening Singapore's equities market

Adjournment Motion3 February 2026 matter-adj-2801

An Adjournment Motion debate in which Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis and Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim set out proposals for Singapore's equities market and Minister Chee Hong Tat responds on the Government's review and measures.

The Minister says the measures aim to make the market more competitive and to increase investor participation, and that MAS will take steps to strengthen investor confidence and enhance investor protection mechanisms, especially for retail investors. He also reports that average daily traded value on SGX grew more than 20% year-on-year to almost $1.8 billion in November 2025, IPO activity raised more than $2.4 billion last year, and SGX total market value crossed $1 trillion.

      MAS and the relevant authorities in Singapore will continue to work closely on robust investigation, market surveillance and timely enforcement against breaches of disclosure requirements and market misconduct.

      The SGX-Nasdaq Global Listing Board, when implemented later this year, will enable eligible companies to simultaneously list on both exchanges with one set of prospectus.

      We are not trying to go for a silver bullet that can, on its own, solve all the problems. There is no magic pill.

      Our goal is to build an equities market where companies sharpen their attention on shareholder value creation, communicate their strategies clearly, optimise capital allocation and thus deliver good shareholder returns.

Open questions from this debate (19)

Questions the debate raises that the record does not resolve. Listed as open questions, not as findings.

  • Whether mandatory value-up disclosure requirements will be introduced, and on what timeline.
  • Whether the Code of Corporate Governance review will result in changes to disclosure rules.
  • How the remaining EQDP funds beyond the $3.95 billion allocated will be deployed.
  • Whether GEMS will be rebalanced toward Catalist listings.
  • Whether family office tax treatment will be refined to require onshore allocations.
  • Whether the SGX-Nasdaq Global Listing Board will be implemented by a specific date.
  • Whether the measures will reverse the decline in market capitalisation described in the debate.
  • Whether retail investor recourse mechanisms will change, and how.
  • Whether Temasek's focus on later-stage investing will affect domestic venture capital liquidity.
  • Whether the Government will adopt the proposed SME tax recognition for listed firms.
  • Whether the proposed tax-free status for employee stock ownerships will be introduced.
  • Whether the CPF Investment Scheme or the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme will be revised to promote local market index ownership.
  • Whether the $30 million grant under the Value Unlock Programme will be expanded.
  • Whether MAS will announce a clear timeline for mandatory disclosures.
  • Whether the review group's recommendations will be implemented in full.
  • Whether the Government will introduce more robust disclosure obligations under Section 199 of the Securities and Futures Act.
  • Whether penalties for false or misleading statements will be increased.
  • Whether the Equity Market Implementation Committee will report publicly on progress.
  • Whether the measures will affect ordinary retail investors' costs or choices.
